newsitem.title: USA: CPUC denies Pacific Bell, GTE California claims.
newsitem.headline: CPUC denies Pacific Bell, GTE California claims.

text.p: The California Public Utilities Commission said on Friday that it rejected requests by Pacific Telesis Group unit Pacific Bell and GTE California for billions of dollars in rate increases.
The increases were sought to make up for the revenues the companies said would be lost due to local phone competition in their service areas, the commission said in a statement.

Pacific Bell sought $3.7 billion over five years. GTE California sought about $500 million. Citizens Utilities Co also joined in arguing for compensation, but did not project a specific loss amount, the commission said.
In rejecting their compensation claims, the commission said the companies' projections were "highly speculative."

The commission said, however, that it would allow the firms to file no earlier than January 1, 1997 an application to show that competition will deprive them of the opportunity to earn a fair return on their regulated assets.

The companies argued that because of the introduction of competition into local phone markets, their shareholders would be denied an opportunity to earn a fair return on investment, amounting to a violation of their claimed constitutional protection against uncompensated "takings" of property.

At the time Pacific Bell and GTE California requested compensation for what they called "franchise impacts," proceedings dealing with major components of a revised regulatory program, such as universal service and equal access rules, had not been completed.

The commission said it would be premature to determine now whether the new regulatory program will adversely affect rates of return. "The companies' testimony, therefore, was found to be too speculative," the commission said.
The commission said it would allow the companies to submit evidence that CPUC policy has resulted in investor losses.
